1.title: Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Storage. It covers the exam area Storage. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Implement storage classes and dynamic volume provisioning. Configure volume types, access modes and reclaim policies. Manage persistent volumes and persistent volume claims. Practice with twelve hands-on labs worth seventy-nine points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Storage (ten percent). Practice in this module: twelve labs, seventy-nine points, about eighty-one minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero (Storage Class standard.

1.title: The storage objects
1.text: The storage objects. The figure shows this: How storage objects bind. Exam tip: A claim binds to a volume by class, access modes and size, and the volume must be at least as large as the claim.

1.title: The storage objects, continued
1.text: The storage objects. Volume (in a Pod spec). Scope: Pod. Job: storage mounted into containers; some types live and die with the Pod. Persistent Volume (P V). Scope: cluster. Job: a piece of storage, made by an admin or by a provisioner. Persistent Volume Claim (P V C). Scope: namespace. Job: a request for storage by a user; binds to one P V (Persistent Volume). Storage Class (S C). Scope: cluster. Job: a recipe for creating P V s on demand (dynamic provisioning). The flow: a Pod references a P V C (Persistent Volume Claim); the P V C binds to a P V (an existing one that fits, or one the Storage Class creates); the kubelet mounts the P V into the Pod.

1.title: Volume types you must know
1.text: Volume types you must know. empty dir. created empty when the Pod starts, deleted with the Pod; scratch space or sharing between containers of one Pod (Lab ten point five). host path. a directory of the node; survives Pod deletion but ties data to one node; avoid except for tests and node agents. config Map, secret, projected. configuration files (Module five). persistent Volume Claim. durable storage through a P V C. nfs, C S I (Container Storage Interface)-driver volumes. network or cloud storage.

1.title: Static provisioning (admin creates the PV)
1.text: Static provisioning (admin creates the P V). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Static provisioning (admin creates the PV), continued
1.text: Static provisioning (admin creates the P V). A claim binds to a P V only when all of these fit: the same storage Class Name; the P V offers (contains) every access mode the claim requests; the P V capacity is at least the requested size (a one gibibyte claim can bind a two gibibytes P V, and then owns all of it). A P V binds to only one claim. A P V C is namespaced; a P V is not. If the P V C omits storage Class Name, the default Storage Class is used. Writing storage Class Name means "no class, bind only to a P V without a class".

1.title: Dynamic provisioning with a StorageClass
1.text: Dynamic provisioning with a Storage Class. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: With Wait For First Consumer a claim stays Pending until a Pod uses it, and that is normal.

1.title: Dynamic provisioning with a StorageClass, continued
1.text: Dynamic provisioning with a Storage Class. provisioner. the driver that creates volumes. reclaim Policy. what happens to the P V when its claim is deleted: Delete (default for S C) or Retain. volume Binding Mode. Immediate creates the volume as soon as the P V C exists; Wait For First Consumer waits until a Pod uses the P V C (so the volume lands on the right node). allow Volume Expansion. whether a P V C may be enlarged later.

1.title: Dynamic provisioning with a StorageClass, continued
1.text: Dynamic provisioning with a Storage Class. Wait For First Consumer explains a P V C that shows Pending with no error: it is waiting for a Pod. Create the Pod and it binds. There must be exactly one default class; change defaults with kube control annotate sc name storageclass dot Kubernetes dot io slash is default class true the overwrite flag (and false on the old one) (Lab ten point three). Look: kube control get sc marks the default with default.

1.title: Access modes and reclaim policies
1.text: Access modes and reclaim policies. Read Write Once. Short: R W O (Read Write Once). Meaning: read-write by one node. Read Only Many. Short: R O X. Meaning: read-only by many nodes. Read Write Many. Short: R W X (Read Write Many). Meaning: read-write by many nodes (needs a driver that supports it, such as N F S (Network File System)). Read Write Once Pod. Short: R W O P. Meaning: read-write by a single Pod. Delete. the P V and the underlying storage are deleted. Retain. the P V stays, status Released, data kept; an admin must clean it before reuse. Exam tip: Change a reclaim policy by patching the P V; Retain keeps the data after the claim is deleted.

1.title: Access modes and reclaim policies, continued
1.text: Access modes and reclaim policies. Change the policy of an existing P V: kube control patch pv name dash p spec persistent Volume Reclaim Policy Retain. Find the P V of a claim: k dash n ns get pvc name dash o json path dot spec dot volume Name (Lab ten point four). The Storage Class reclaim Policy only affects P V s created afterwards.

1.title: Use a PVC in a Pod
1.text: Use a P V C in a Pod. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Use a PVC in a Pod, continued
1.text: Use a P V C in a Pod. The P V C must be in the same namespace as the Pod. Data written to a bound P V C survives deletion of the Pod.

1.title: Troubleshooting storage (break-and-fix patterns)
1.text: Troubleshooting storage (break-and-fix patterns). Pod Pending, event "unbound immediate Persistent Volume Claims" or "persistentvolumeclaim not found". Look at: kube control describe pod, kube control get pvc. Typical cause: P V C missing, wrong name or wrong namespace. P V C Pending, event "storageclass... not found". Look at: kube control describe pvc, kube control get sc. Typical cause: class name typo (Lab ten point six). P V C Pending, no matching P V. Look at: kube control describe pvc, kube control get pv. Typical cause: access mode not offered by the P V, size too big, class mismatch (Lab ten point seven). P V C Pending and nothing else. Look at: kube control get sc. Typical cause: Wait For First Consumer: create the Pod. P V Released. Look at: kube control get pv. Typical cause: claim deleted with Retain; remove claim Ref to reuse. Exam tip: A claim cannot be fixed in place: delete it and create it again.

1.title: Troubleshooting storage (break-and-fix patterns), continued
1.text: Troubleshooting storage (break-and-fix patterns). A claim's storage Class Name, access Modes and size cannot be changed on a bound or pending claim in the ways these tasks need: delete and recreate the claim (and the Pod using it).

2.title: Lab 10.4: reclaim retain
2.text: Lab ten point four: reclaim retain. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace st four, the Persistent Volume Claim keepme is bound to a dynamically provisioned Persistent Volume whose reclaim policy is Delete. The data must survive even if the claim is deleted. Change the reclaim policy of that Persistent Volume to Retain. Do not change the claim or the Storage Class. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.4: reclaim retain, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run pv kube control dash n st four get pvc keepme dash o json path dot spec dot volume Name. Then kube control get pv pv. Then kube control patch pv pv dash p spec persistent Volume Reclaim Policy Retain. Then kube control get pv pv. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

Both mount the volume at slash shared. The volume must be an empty dir (it is deleted with the Pod). Prove that consumer can read the file. 2.title: Lab 10.6: fix pending pvc
2.text: Lab ten point six: fix pending pvc. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace st six, the Pod app is stuck Pending because its Persistent Volume Claim app data does not bind. Find the cause and fix it so the Pod runs with the claim bound. Keep the names app and app data, the size one gibibyte and Read Write Once. (A claim's Storage Class cannot be edited in place; recreate what is needed.). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n st six describe pod app then pipe to grep dash i -A two Failed Scheduling. Then kube control dash n st six describe pvc app data then pipe to grep dash i -A two events. Then kube control get sc. Then kube control dash n st six delete pod app the force flag the grace period flag zero. Then kube control dash n st six delete pvc app data. kube control dash n st six apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

3.title: Recall Check 1
3.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What decides whether a P V C binds to a P V? Answer: Same Storage Class, the P V offers all requested access modes, and the P V capacity is at least the requested size. Question two. What does volume Binding Mode Wait For First Consumer do? Answer: It delays creating and binding the volume until a Pod uses the P V C. Question three. What happens to a P V with Retain when its P V C is deleted? Answer: The P V stays with status Released and keeps its data.

3.title: Recall Check 2
3.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which volume type is deleted when the Pod is deleted? Answer: empty dir. Question five. How do you make a Storage Class the default? Answer: Annotate it storageclass dot Kubernetes dot io slash is default class true (and remove the mark from the old default). Question six. Can a P V be bound by two claims? Answer: No, one claim only.

3.title: Recall Check 3
3.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. A P V C requests Read Write Once but the only P V offers Read Write Many. What happens? Answer: It stays Pending: the P V does not offer the requested mode. Question eight. What is the effect of a missing storage Class Name in a P V C? Answer: The default Storage Class is used.

3.title: Module Recap
3.text: Here is the recap. Objects: P V (cluster), P V C (namespace), Storage Class (recipe). Bind rules: class plus access modes plus size (P V greater than equals claim). Dynamic: Storage Class with provisioner; default class by annotation. Binding mode: Wait For First Consumer equals Pending until a Pod uses it. Reclaim: Delete or Retain; patch the P V to change it. Access modes: R W O, R O X, R W X, R W O P. empty dir: lives with the Pod; host path ties data to a node. Fix a claim: delete and recreate it. In the next module, we continue the course.
